props.headline: One Data Layer for Every Kind of Scale
props.subheadline: Our mission is to make sure the database is never what holds a team back. Applications grow, data piles up, and AI agents now create databases faster than any team could. TiDB is one open-source data layer that scales with all of it, without sharding, rewrites, or giving up consistency.

items.content:
For years, teams have stitched databases together to keep up: sharding MySQL by hand, splitting transactions from analytics, adding a new system for every new need. Each fix adds another thing to run.

Now AI agents are adding a new kind of scale on top. In the last six months, 99% of the databases on TiDB Cloud Starter were created by agents, not people.

Both paths lead to the same need: one data layer for transactions, analytics, and vectors that scales from a single small instance to millions of them, and from gigabytes to petabytes, without a rewrite. That's what we build.

In 2015, three infrastructure engineers were tired of how databases were managed at large internet companies. Every time an application grew, managing, scaling, and maintaining the database took far more effort than it should have.

They looked for a database that could grow with the application without that pain. They didn't find one. So they started building it, in the open, and named the company PingCAP.

That project became TiDB. All three co-founders still lead the company today.

Max Liu, co-founder and CEO

Ed Huang, co-founder and CTO

Dylan Cui, co-founder

Open source wasn't a decision we made later. TiDB was open from the first commit, and it still is. Hundreds of contributors around the world help build it, and TiKV, the storage engine underneath TiDB, is a graduated project of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.

Working in the open keeps us honest. Anyone can read the code, question a design choice, or fix something we missed. By the end of 2026, we plan to open source the core of TiDB X, our newest architecture, so the next version of TiDB is built the same way the first one was.

> "Open source is in our DNA. TiDB has been open since day one, and we believe it's the best way to collaborate and the fastest way to innovate."

Max Liu, co-founder and CEO

props.title: Built Alongside the People Who Run It

items.content:
The hardest problems we've worked on came from customers who wouldn't accept a limit. Atlassian runs Jira and Confluence for tens of millions of people on systems that can never go down. Pinterest, Plaid, Flipkart, and many others brought workloads their previous databases struggled to handle.

Each of them pushed TiDB further than we would have on our own, and we still build it that way: alongside the engineers who depend on it.

> "Storage could no longer be an afterthought managed team by team. It had to become a first-class internal platform. TiDB proved to be the platform that ticked all of those boxes."

Vinod Kumar, Atlassian, speaking at TiDB SCaiLE 2026
